newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX POWER SEEN LOWER AFTER MONDAY LIGHT SELLOFF.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX POWER SEEN LOWER AFTER MONDAY LIGHT SELLOFF.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Tuesday, continuing a light sell-off that reduced Monday's early gains tied to shortcovering and steady western physical prices, market sources said.
"We're seeing some follow-through (selling) here," a Houston futures trader said.

In over-the-counter business, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $31.10-31.60 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Monday's settlement at $31.81, and September California-Oregon Border (COB) was discussed at $23.30-23.60 a MWh versus yesterday's close at $23.60.
In early cash activity, firm peak deliveries for Wednesday at the Palo Verde switchyard in Arizona were talked at $40.00-43.00 a MWh, while those at COB at $20.00-22.00.

Given yesterday's weak close, analysts pegged chart resistance for September PV at $33.00 and for September COB at $24.25. On the downside, they assessed technical support for September PV at $30.25 and for September COB at $22.55.

Forecasters said scattered showers and thunderstorms were expected to keep temperatures cool in the northeastern part of the Southwest. Readings for the rest of the region would run normal to slightly above normal.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average below normal across most of the region with the exception of the far west area which would run slightly above than normal.
The 670 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Centralia coal-fired power station in Washington state was tentatively set to shut Monday for a two-day outage.
A 700 MW unit at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was heard shut last Friday for repairs, and expected to resume operation today.

The 750 MW unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power station near Page, Ariz., was scheduled to restart Monday afternoon after being shut over the weekend for repairs. Navajo's other two 750 MW units were said to be operating normally.

Separately, southbound transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie will be cut by 350 MW to 850 MW during certain hours on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of this week, according to the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).
